sentences.zh: 魯炅魯炅，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Jiong, Lu Jiong, was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jiong was a native of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺餘，涉獵書史。

translations.literal: His height was more than seven chi, and he ranged widely through books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He stood over seven chi tall and had read widely in history and the classics.

sentences.zh: ，隴右節度使哥舒翰引為別奏。

translations.literal: [In the sixth year of Tianbao,] the Longyou military commissioner Geshu Han brought him in as a special memorialist.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao, Geshu Han, military commissioner of Longyou, took him on as a special memorialist.

sentences.zh: 顏真卿為監察御史，使至隴右，翰嘗設宴，真卿謂翰曰：「中丞自郎將授將軍，便登節制，後生可畏，得無人乎？

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing served as investigating censor and was sent to Longyou; Han once held a banquet, and Zhenqing said to Han, "The Commissioner rose from commandant to general and at once attained a commission—later generations are to be feared; are there not men [among them]?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhenqing was investigating censor on a mission to Longyou, Geshu Han once gave a banquet. Zhenqing said to him, "You went from commandant to general and straightway received a commission—the young are formidable. Surely you have capable men among them?"

sentences.zh: 」炅時立在階下，翰指炅曰：「此人後當為節度使矣。

translations.literal: " Jiong was then standing below the steps; Han pointed to Jiong and said, "This man will later become a military commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: " Jiong was standing below the steps at the time. Han pointed to him and said, "This man will one day be a military commissioner."

sentences.zh: 」後以隴右破吐蕃跳蕩功，累授右領軍大將軍同正員，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: " Later, for merit in defeating the Tibetan Tiaodang band in Longyou, he was repeatedly promoted to Right Army General of the Courageous Guards, acting full appointee, and was granted a purple-gold fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, for his service in defeating the Tibetan Tiaodang rebels in Longyou, he rose through successive appointments to Right Army General of the Courageous Guards with acting full rank and received a purple-gold fish tally.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，選任將帥。

translations.literal: At the rebellion of An Lushan, commanders were selected and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, the court began appointing generals.

sentences.zh: 十五載正月，拜炅上洛太守，未行，遷南陽太守、本郡守捉，仍充防禦使。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year [of Tianbao], Jiong was appointed Grand Warden of Shangluo; before he departed he was transferred to Grand Warden of Nanyang, local commander for the commandery, and also made defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 750, Jiong was named grand warden of Shangluo. Before he could take up the post he was moved to grand warden of Nanyang, with command of the commandery's defense forces, and also made defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋兼御史大夫，充南陽節度使，以嶺南、黔中、山南東道子弟五萬人屯葉縣北，滍水之南，築柵，四面掘壕以自固。

translations.literal: Soon he was also made Grand Censor and installed as Nanyang military commissioner; with fifty thousand troops of the Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Shannan East circuits he encamped north of Ye County and south of the Zhi River, built palisades, and dug moats on all four sides to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the additional title of grand censor and made military commissioner of Nanyang. He stationed fifty thousand troops drawn from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and eastern Shannan north of Ye County and south of the Zhi River, built stockades, and dug trenches on every side to fortify his position.

sentences.zh: 至五月，賊將武令珣、畢思琛等來擊之，眾欲出戰，炅不許。

translations.literal: By the fifth month, the rebel generals Wu Lingxun, Bi Sichen, and others came to attack; the troops wished to go out and fight, but Jiong would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the rebel generals Wu Lingxun and Bi Sichen attacked. The men wanted to sally out, but Jiong refused.

sentences.zh: 賊於營西順風燒煙，營內坐立不得，橫門扇及木爭出，賊矢集如雨，炅與中使薛道等挺身遁走，余眾盡沒。

translations.literal: The rebels burned smoke upwind on the west of the camp; inside the camp men could neither sit nor stand; they scrambled for the crossbars of the gates and for timber to get out; rebel arrows fell thick as rain; Jiong, the palace envoy Xue Dao, and others threw themselves forward and fled, and the rest of the force was entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels set smoke fires upwind on the west side of the camp. Inside, soldiers could neither sit nor stand and fought to get through the gate bars and over the palisades. Rebel arrows fell like rain. Jiong, the palace envoy Xue Dao, and others broke out and fled; the rest of the army was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 嶺南節度使何履光、黔中節度使趙國珍、襄陽太守徐浩未至，裨將嶺南、黔中、荊襄子弟半在軍，多懷金銀為資糧，軍資器械盡棄於路如山積。

translations.literal: The Lingnan military commissioner He Luguang, the Qianzhong military commissioner Zhao Guozhen, and the Xiangyang grand warden Xu Hao had not yet arrived; half the subordinate officers and troops of Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jing-Xiang origin were in the army; many carried gold and silver as provisions; military supplies and weapons were all abandoned on the road in heaps like hills.
translations.idiomatic: The Lingnan commissioner He Luguang, the Qianzhong commissioner Zhao Guozhen, and the Xiangyang grand warden Xu Hao had not yet arrived. Half the army consisted of junior officers and men from Lingnan, Qianzhong, and the Jing-Xiang region, many of whom carried gold and silver as personal stores. Arms, equipment, and supplies were abandoned along the road in hill-high piles.

sentences.zh: 至是賊徒不勝其富。

translations.literal: At this the rebels could not bear [the sight of] such wealth.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels could scarcely cope with such sudden riches.

sentences.zh: 炅收合殘卒，保南陽郡，為賊所圍。

translations.literal: Jiong gathered the remnant troops and held Nanyang commandery, and was besieged by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong rallied the survivors and held Nanyang, where the rebels soon besieged him.

sentences.zh: 尋而潼關失守，賊使哥舒翰招之，不從。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Tong Pass fell; the rebels sent Geshu Han to summon him, and he would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Tong Pass fell, the rebels sent the captured Geshu Han to win him over, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 又使偽將豫州刺史武令珣等攻之，累月不能克。

translations.literal: They again sent the false [Yan] general, Prefect of Yuzhou Wu Lingxun, and others to attack him; for many months they could not take [the city].
translations.idiomatic: They then sent the rebel general Wu Lingxun, nominal prefect of Yuzhou, and others against him, but for months they could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 武令珣死，又令田承嗣攻之。

translations.literal: Wu Lingxun died, and [the rebels] again ordered Tian Chengsi to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Lingxun died, they put Tian Chengsi in command of the siege.

sentences.zh: 潁川太守來瑱、襄陽太守魏仲犀合勢救之。

translations.literal: The Yingchuan grand warden Lai Zhen and the Xiangyang grand warden Wei Zhongxi joined forces to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingchuan grand warden Lai Zhen and the Xiangyang grand warden Wei Zhongxi combined their forces to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 犀使弟孟馴為將，領兵至明府橋，望賊而走，眾遂大敗。

translations.literal: Zhongxi sent his younger brother Mengxun as general; he led troops to Mingfu Bridge, saw the rebels and fled, and the army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi sent his younger brother Mengxun to command the relief force. At Mingfu Bridge Mengxun caught sight of the enemy and fled, and the army was routed.

sentences.zh: 炅城中食盡，煮牛皮筋角而食之，米鬥至四五十千，有價無米，鼠一頭至四百文，餓死者相枕藉。

translations.literal: Food in Jiong's city was exhausted; they boiled ox hide, sinew, and horn to eat; a dou of rice reached forty or fifty thousand [cash]; there was a price but no rice; one rat fetched four hundred cash; the starved lay dead piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions in the city ran out. The defenders boiled ox hide, sinew, and horn for food. A dou of rice was priced at forty or fifty thousand cash, yet none could be bought. A single rat sold for four hundred cash. The dead from starvation lay in heaps.

sentences.zh: 肅宗使中官將軍曹日昇來宣慰，路絕不得入。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong sent the eunuch general Cao Risheng to proclaim consolation [to the garrison]; the roads were cut off and he could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong sent the eunuch general Cao Risheng with imperial words of encouragement, but the roads were blocked and he could not reach the city.

sentences.zh: 日昇請單騎入致命，仲犀曰：「不可，賊若擒吾敕使，我亦何安！

translations.literal: Risheng asked to enter alone on horseback to deliver the edict; Zhongxi said, "It cannot be done—if the rebels seize our imperial messenger, how can I be at ease!"
translations.idiomatic: Risheng asked to ride in alone and deliver the message. Zhongxi objected: "No. If the rebels capture our imperial envoy, how can I answer for it?"

sentences.zh: 」顏真卿適自河北次於襄陽，謂仲犀曰：「曹使既果決，不顧萬死之地，何得沮之！

translations.literal: " Yan Zhenqing happened to have come from Hebei and was encamped at Xiangyang; he said to Zhongxi, "Commissioner Cao is already resolute and does not regard a place of ten thousand deaths—how can you thwart him!"
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Zhenqing had just arrived from Hebei and was stationed at Xiangyang. He told Zhongxi, "Commissioner Cao is determined to go and does not fear death. How can you stop him?"

sentences.zh: 縱為賊所獲，是亡一使者；

translations.literal: Even if he is taken by the rebels, that is the loss of one envoy;
translations.idiomatic: Even if the rebels seize him, that is only the loss of one envoy;

sentences.zh: 敬得入城，則萬人之心固矣。

translations.literal: if respectfully he can enter the city, then the hearts of ten thousand men will be made firm.
translations.idiomatic: but if he reaches the city, the hearts of ten thousand defenders will be steadied.

sentences.zh: 公何愛焉？

translations.literal: Why, sir, do you begrudge [this]?
translations.idiomatic: Why would you withhold him?

sentences.zh: 」中官馮廷環曰：「將軍必能入，我請以兩騎助之。

translations.literal: " The eunuch Feng Tinghuan said, "The general will surely be able to enter; I ask to assist him with two horsemen."
translations.idiomatic: " The eunuch Feng Tinghuan said, "The general will get through—I will lend him two horsemen."

sentences.zh: 」日昇又自有傔騎數人，仲犀又以數騎共十人同行。

translations.literal: " Risheng also had several of his own attendant horsemen; Zhongxi added several more horsemen, and ten men went together.
translations.idiomatic: " Risheng had several personal escorts of his own, and Zhongxi added a few more so that ten men rode in together.

sentences.zh: 賊徒望見，知其驍銳，不敢逼。

translations.literal: The rebels saw them from afar, knew them to be fierce and sharp, and did not dare press them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels saw them from a distance, recognized how formidable they were, and did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 日昇既入城，炅眾初以為望絕，忽有使來宣命，皆踴躍一心。

translations.literal: Once Risheng had entered the city, Jiong's troops had at first thought hope was cut off; suddenly an envoy came to proclaim the edict, and all leaped for joy with one heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Risheng reached the city, Jiong's men had thought all hope lost. The sudden arrival of an imperial messenger revived them, and the garrison rallied as one.

sentences.zh: 日昇以其十人至襄陽取糧，賊雖追之，不敢擊，遂以一千人取音聲路運糧而入，賊亦不能遏，又得相持數月。

translations.literal: Risheng with his ten men went to Xiangyang to fetch grain; though the rebels pursued, they did not dare strike; then with one thousand men he took the Yinsheng route to transport grain in; the rebels also could not stop him, and [the garrison] was able to hold out several months more.
translations.idiomatic: Risheng and his ten companions went to Xiangyang for grain. The rebels followed but did not dare attack. He then sent a thousand men along the Yinsheng road to bring supplies into the city, and the rebels could not stop them either. The siege dragged on for several months more.

sentences.zh: 炅在圍中一年，救兵不至，晝夜苦戰，人相食。

translations.literal: Jiong was in the siege for one year; relief troops did not arrive; day and night they fought bitterly; men ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong remained under siege for a year. No relief force came. The defenders fought day and night, until men began to eat one another.

sentences.zh: 五月十五日，率眾持滿傳矢突圍而出南陽，投襄陽。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the fifth month he led the masses, bows drawn and arrows passed [along the line], to burst through the encirclement and leave Nanyang, and threw himself on Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the fifth month he led his men out of Nanyang with bows strung and arrows passed hand to hand, broke through the encirclement, and withdrew to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 田承嗣來追，苦戰二日，殺賊甚眾。

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi came in pursuit; they fought bitterly for two days and killed very many rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi pursued them. For two days they fought fiercely and killed a great many rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊又知其決死，遂不敢逼，朝廷因除御史大夫、襄陽節度使。

translations.literal: The rebels again knew that [the Tang troops] were resolved to die, and so did not dare press them; the court thereupon removed [his former titles and] appointed him Grand Censor and Xiangyang military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Tang troops would fight to the death, the rebels no longer pressed the pursuit. The court then appointed Jiong grand censor and military commissioner of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 時賊志欲南侵江、漢，賴炅奮命扼其沖要，南夏所以保全。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels' intent was to invade south into the Jiang and Han [regions]; it was by relying on Jiong's exerting his life to choke their strategic points that southern Xia was thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then intended to push south into the Yangzi and Han river country. Jiong's desperate defense of the key passes is what preserved the southern provinces.

sentences.zh: 十月，王師收兩京，承嗣、令珣等奔於河北。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the imperial army recovered the two capitals; Chengsi, Lingxun, and others fled to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the imperial armies recaptured the two capitals, and Chengsi, Lingxun, and the other rebel commanders fled to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 南陽遭大亂之後，距鄧州二百里，人煙斷絕，遺骸委積於墻塹間。

translations.literal: After Nanyang suffered the great disorder, for two hundred li toward Dengzhou human smoke was cut off, and abandoned corpses lay heaped between walls and moats.
translations.idiomatic: After the great upheaval, Nanyang and the two hundred li toward Dengzhou were depopulated, with corpses heaped along the walls and in the ditches.

sentences.zh: 十二月，策勛行賞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, merit was assessed and rewards distributed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the court reviewed achievements and issued rewards.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「特進、太僕卿、南陽郡守、兼御史大夫、權知襄陽節度事、上柱國、金鄉縣公魯炅，蘊是韜略，副茲節制，竭節保邦，悉心陷敵。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Special Advancement, Grand Master of the Stud, Grand Warden of Nanyang commandery, concurrent Grand Censor, acting Xiangyang military commissioner, Supreme Pillar of State, Duke of Jinxiang county Lu Jiong—he harbors strategy and tactics, assists this commission, exhausts his integrity to preserve the state, and devotes his heart to striking the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Lu Jiong, special advancement holder, grand master of the stud, grand warden of Nanyang, concurrent grand censor, acting military commissioner of Xiangyang, supreme pillar of state, and duke of Jinxiang—steeped in strategy, faithful to his commission, he has exhausted himself to defend the realm and thrown himself wholly against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 表之旗幟，分以土田。

translations.literal: Let banners be displayed for him and land and fields be allotted.
translations.idiomatic: Let his banners be raised in honor and lands be granted him."

sentences.zh: 可開府儀同三司、兼御史大夫，封岐國公，食實封二百戶，兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: He may be made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the status of Three Excellencies, concurrent Grand Censor, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi state, with an actual fief of two hundred households, and concurrent Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He is approved as grand master of splendid happiness with the privileges of the three excellencies, concurrent grand censor, enfeoffed as duke of Qi with an actual fief of two hundred households, and concurrent metropolitan governor of Jingzhao."

sentences.zh: ，兼鄭州刺史，充鄭、陳、潁、亳等州節度使。

translations.literal: [He was also made] concurrent Prefect of Zhengzhou and installed as military commissioner of Zheng, Chen, Ying, Bo, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made prefect of Zhengzhou and military commissioner over Zheng, Chen, Ying, Bo, and the other prefectures in his circuit.

sentences.zh: ，為淮西襄陽節度使、鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: [He was] made Huai-West and Xiangyang military commissioner and Prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed military commissioner of Huai-West and Xiangyang and prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，與朔方節度使司徒郭子儀、河東節度使太尉李光弼等九節度同圍安慶緒於相州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, together with the Shuofang military commissioner, Minister of Education Guo Ziyi, the Hedong military commissioner, Grand Marshal Li Guangbi, and eight other commissioners, he jointly besieged An Qingxu at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he joined Guo Ziyi of Shuofang, Li Guangbi of Hedong, and seven other commissioners in besieging An Qingxu at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 炅領淮西、襄陽節度行營步卒萬人、馬軍三百，以李抱玉為兵馬使，炅分界知東面之北。

translations.literal: Jiong led ten thousand infantry and three hundred cavalry of the Huai-West and Xiangyang circuit campaign headquarters; Li Baoyu was made army-and-horse commissioner; Jiong's assigned sector was to know the north of the eastern face.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong commanded ten thousand foot soldiers and three hundred horsemen of the Huai-West and Xiangyang field army, with Li Baoyu as his army commissioner. His sector lay on the northern part of the eastern front.

sentences.zh: 二年六月六日，賊將史思明自范陽來救，戰於安陽河北，王師不利，炅中流矢奔退。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the sixth month of the second year [of Qianyuan], the rebel general Shi Siming came from Fanyang to relieve [An Qingxu]; they fought on the north bank of the Anyang River; the imperial army was unfavorable; Jiong was struck by a flowing arrow and fled in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the sixth month of 759 the rebel Shi Siming marched from Fanyang to relieve the siege. The armies clashed north of the Anyang River. The imperial forces were defeated, and Jiong, wounded by an arrow, fled.

sentences.zh: 時諸節度以回紇戰敗，因而退散，盡棄軍糧器械，所過虜掠，炅兵士剽奪尤甚，人因驚怨。

translations.literal: At that time the various commissioners, because the Uyghurs had been defeated in battle, thereupon dispersed in retreat, entirely abandoning army grain and weapons; wherever they passed they plundered; Jiong's soldiers plundered and seized especially severely, and the people were thereby alarmed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghur allies were beaten, the commissioners broke and fell back, abandoning grain and arms along the route and plundering the countryside. Jiong's troops looted more savagely than any, and popular resentment boiled over.

sentences.zh: 五日，至新鄭縣，聞郭子儀已整眾屯谷水，李光弼還太原，炅憂懼，仰藥而卒。

translations.literal: On the fifth day [of the month] he reached Xinzheng county; he heard that Guo Ziyi had already reorganized his troops and was encamped at Gu River, and that Li Guangbi had returned to Taiyuan; Jiong was anxious and fearful, took poison looking upward, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later he reached Xinzheng. Learning that Guo Ziyi had regrouped at Gu River and that Li Guangbi had withdrawn to Taiyuan, he gave way to despair and took poison.

sentences.zh: 裴裴，以門廕入仕，累遷京兆府司錄參軍。

translations.literal: Pei Chong, Pei Chong, entered office through hereditary privilege and was repeatedly promoted to Registrar of the Metropolitan Prefecture of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Chong entered government through hereditary privilege and rose to registrar of the metropolitan prefecture of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 來瑱鎮陜州，引為判官；

translations.literal: When Lai Zhen governed Shaan prefecture, [Zhen] brought him in as administrative aide;
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Zhen was posted to Shaan prefecture, he took Pei on as his administrative aide;

sentences.zh: 瑱移襄州，又為瑱行軍司馬，瑱遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: when Zhen moved to Xiangzhou, [Pei] again served as Zhen's campaign army marshal; Zhen treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: and when Zhen moved to Xiangzhou, made him his campaign marshal. Zhen treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 及瑱淮西之敗，逗留不行，密表聞奏。

translations.literal: When Zhen was defeated in Huai-West, [Pei] lingered and did not go; he secretly memorialized to inform the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhen's defeat in Huai-West, Pei lingered behind the army and sent a secret memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以瑱掌重兵，惡之，密詔以代瑱為襄州刺史，充防禦使。

translations.literal: The court, because Zhen held heavy troops, hated him, and in a secret edict ordered [Pei] to replace Zhen as Prefect of Xiangzhou and to serve as defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court, uneasy that Zhen commanded so large a force, issued a secret order appointing Pei prefect of Xiangzhou and defense commissioner in his place.

sentences.zh: 本鎮谷城，及受密命，乃率麾下二千人赴襄陽。

translations.literal: He had originally garrisoned Gucheng; on receiving the secret command he then led two thousand men under his command to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pei had been stationed at Gucheng. On receiving the secret order he marched two thousand men to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 時瑱亦奉詔依舊任，瑱遂設具於江津以俟之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhen also received an edict to resume his former post; Zhen thereupon set out provisions at the river ford to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had also received orders to keep his post. He laid out a feast at the river crossing to receive Pei.

sentences.zh: 初聲言假道入朝，及見瑱，即雲奉代，且欲視事。

translations.literal: At first he declared that he was only borrowing the route to enter court; when he saw Zhen, he at once said he had come to replace [him] and wished to take up office.
translations.idiomatic: At first Pei claimed he was only passing through on his way to court. Once he met Zhen, he announced that he had come to replace him and intended to take office at once.

sentences.zh: 瑱報曰：「瑱已奉恩命復任此。

translations.literal: Zhen replied, saying, "Zhen has already received the gracious command to resume this post."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen replied, "I have already received the emperor's order to resume this post."

sentences.zh: 」惶惑，喻其麾下曰：「此言必妄。

translations.literal: " [Pei] was alarmed and bewildered; he instructed his subordinates, saying, "These words must be false."
translations.idiomatic: " Pei was thrown into confusion. He told his men, "That cannot be true."

sentences.zh: 」遂引射瑱軍，因與瑱兵交戰，大敗，士卒死傷殆盡。

translations.literal: " He thereupon drew [his men] to shoot at Zhen's army; thus he joined battle with Zhen's troops; [Pei] was utterly defeated, and soldiers were killed and wounded almost to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: " He then opened fire on Zhen's troops. In the fighting that followed Pei was routed and his force was nearly annihilated.

sentences.zh: 走還谷城舊營，瑱追擒之。

translations.literal: [Pei] fled back to his old camp at Gucheng; Zhen pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei fled back to his old camp at Gucheng, but Zhen pursued and captured him.

sentences.zh: 朝旨務安漢南，乃歸咎於。

translations.literal: The court's intent was to secure peace in southern Han, and blame was therefore laid on [Pei].
translations.idiomatic: Because the court wished to pacify the Han River south, the blame was laid on Pei.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年七月，敕曰：「前襄州刺史裴，性本頑疏，行惟狂悖。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Baoying, an edict said: "The former Prefect of Xiangzhou Pei [Chong]'s nature is fundamentally obstinate and crude, his conduct solely arrogant and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 762 an edict declared: "The former prefect of Xiangzhou, Pei Chong, is by nature coarse and stupid and in conduct reckless and rebellious.

sentences.zh: 頃因試用，爰委軍戎，守在要沖，無聞方略。

translations.literal: Recently, because of a trial appointment, military affairs were entrusted to him; he guarded a strategic pass, yet no strategy was heard of.
translations.idiomatic: He was recently given a trial command on a vital frontier, yet showed no sign of competent strategy.

sentences.zh: 所以申命來瑱，重撫漢南，即宜奔赴闕廷，謝其曠職。

translations.literal: Therefore orders were issued to Lai Zhen to reassure southern Han anew; [Pei] should at once hurry to the court gate and answer for his neglect of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zhen was therefore ordered back to reassure the Han River south, and Pei should have gone to court at once to answer for his failure.

sentences.zh: 而乃顧惜名位，輕圖異端，誣構忠良，妄興兵甲。

translations.literal: Yet he clung to name and rank, lightly plotted heterodoxy, falsely framed loyal and good men, and wantonly raised arms.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he clung to office, plotted rebellion, slandered a loyal commander, and rashly took up arms.

sentences.zh: 遽令追召，敢欲逗留，是有無君之心，不唯罔上之罪。

translations.literal: He was suddenly ordered to be summoned back, yet dared to wish to linger—this is a heart without a lord, not only the crime of deceiving superiors.
translations.idiomatic: When recalled he dared to delay. That is disloyalty to the throne, not merely disobedience.

sentences.zh: 又轉輸之物，軍國所資，擅為費用，其數甚廣。

translations.literal: Moreover, transport goods—the resources of army and state—he appropriated for his own use on a very wide scale.
translations.idiomatic: He also misappropriated on a large scale the transport supplies on which army and state depend.

sentences.zh: 據其抵犯，合置嚴誅。

translations.literal: According to his offenses, he ought to receive severe execution.
translations.idiomatic: By rights his crimes call for execution.

sentences.zh: 但自朕登極已來，屢施恩宥，肆諸朝市，所未忍為。

translations.literal: But since I ascended the throne I have repeatedly extended gracious pardon; to expose [offenders] in the market of the court is what I have not yet been willing to do.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since my accession I have often shown mercy, and I am unwilling to expose him in the public market.

sentences.zh: 宜寬殊死之刑，俾就投荒之謫，宜除名，長流費州。

translations.literal: He should be granted leniency from the penalty of extraordinary death and be made to undergo banishment to the wilds; his name should be struck off and he should be exiled far to Fei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Let the death penalty be commuted to exile in the far south: strip him of rank and banish him permanently to Fei prefecture."

sentences.zh: 器局輕褊，初興師徒，給用無節。

translations.literal: [Chong's] capacity and bearing were light and narrow; when he first raised troops, expenditures were without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Pei was shallow and impulsive. When he first raised troops he spent without limit.

sentences.zh: 及敗撓，遲回赴召，將至京師，會有是命。

translations.literal: When he was defeated and broken, he delayed in answering the summons; as he was about to reach the capital, this edict happened [to arrive].
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat he dragged his feet answering the recall. Just as he neared the capital, this edict overtook him.

sentences.zh: 既行，至藍田驛，賜自盡。

translations.literal: Once he had set out, when he reached Lantian post station he was granted permission to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: On the road, at Lantian post station, he was ordered to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 來瑱來瑱，邠州永壽人也。

translations.literal: Lai Zhen, Lai Zhen, was a native of Yongshou in Bin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zhen was a native of Yongshou in Bin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父曜，起於卒伍。

translations.literal: His father Yao rose from the ranks of soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao had risen from the ranks.

sentences.zh: ，為鴻臚卿同正員、安西副都護、持節磧西副大使、四鎮節度使，後為右領軍大將軍、仗內五坊等使，名著西陲。

translations.literal: [In the eighteenth year of Kaiyuan] he was made Grand Master of the Court for Diplomatic Relations, acting full appointee, Vice Protector-General of Anxi, Deputy Commissioner with staff for the Western Regions, military commissioner of the Four Garrisons; later he was Right Army General of the Courageous Guards and commissioner of the Five Parks within the palace guard; his fame was renowned on the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In 730 he became grand master of the court for diplomatic relations, vice protector-general of Anxi, deputy commissioner for the Western Regions, and military commissioner of the Four Garrisons. He later served as right army general of the Courageous Guards and commissioner of the palace parks, and won great fame on the western frontier.

sentences.zh: ，以子貴，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: [In the first year of Baoying,] because of his son's eminence, [Yao] was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 762, because of his son's distinction, he was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 瑱少尚名節，慷慨有大志，頗涉書傳。

translations.literal: Zhen in youth esteemed reputation and integrity, was generous and had great resolve, and ranged considerably through books and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Zhen prized honor, was bold and ambitious, and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，四鎮從職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he followed [his father] in service at the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he followed his father on campaign in the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 十一載，為左贊善大夫、殿中侍御史，充伊西、北庭行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year [of Tianbao] he was made Left Mentor to the Heir Apparent, Palace Attendant Censor, and campaign army marshal for Yixi and Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: In 752 he was appointed left mentor to the heir apparent, palace attendant censor, and campaign marshal for Yixi and Beiting.

sentences.zh: 玄宗詔朝臣舉智謀果決、才堪統眾者各一人。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered the court ministers each to recommend one man of wisdom and stratagem, resolute and decisive, whose talent could command the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong ordered each court official to recommend one man who was resourceful, resolute, and fit to command troops.

sentences.zh: 拾遺張鎬薦瑱有縱橫之略，臨事能斷，堪當禦悔之任。

translations.literal: The Remonstrance Official Zhang Gao recommended Zhen as having vertical-and-horizontal strategy, able to decide affairs on the spot, fit to undertake the charge of warding off regret.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance official Zhang Gao recommended Zhen as a master of strategy who could act decisively in crisis and was fit to bear the burden of national defense.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，以孝聞。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned her with a filial devotion that won wide notice.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，張垍復薦之，起復兼汝南郡太守，未行，改潁川太守。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Zhang Ya again recommended him; he was recalled from mourning and made concurrent Grand Warden of Runan commandery; before he departed he was changed to Grand Warden of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Zhang Ya recommended him again. Recalled from mourning, he was named grand warden of Runan, then reassigned to Yingchuan before he could take up either post.

sentences.zh: 賊攻之。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked the city.

sentences.zh: 城中積粟素多，瑱繕修有備。

translations.literal: Stored grain in the city had always been abundant; Zhen repaired [the defenses] and was prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The city had long held ample grain stores, and Zhen had repaired the defenses in good time.

sentences.zh: 賊繼至城下，瑱親射之，無不應弦而斃。

translations.literal: The rebels came in succession to below the wall; Zhen personally shot them, and none failed to fall dead at the twang of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel assaults followed one after another. Zhen shot from the walls himself, and every arrow found its mark.

sentences.zh: 賊使降將畢思琛招瑱，琛即瑱父曜故將，城下拜泣吊瑱，瑱不應。

translations.literal: The rebels sent the surrendered general Bi Sichen to summon Zhen; Chen was formerly Yao's old officer under Zhen's father; below the wall he bowed and wept in condolence to Zhen; Zhen did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent the defector Bi Sichen, once an officer under Zhen's father, to win him over. Below the wall Chen bowed and wept as though mourning him. Zhen would not answer.

sentences.zh: 前後殺賊頗眾，鹹呼瑱為「來嚼鐵」。

translations.literal: Before and after he killed quite many rebels; all called Zhen "Lai Chews Iron."
translations.idiomatic: He killed a great many rebels in these fights, and men nicknamed him "Lai Chews Iron."

sentences.zh: 以功加銀青光祿大夫，攝御史中丞、本郡防禦使及河南淮南遊奕逐要招討等使。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Vice Censor-in-Chief, defense commissioner of his home commandery, and commissioner for Henan, Huainan, mobile patrol, pursuit of key points, recruitment, and suppression, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to silver-gleam grand master of splendid happiness, acting vice censor-in-chief, defense commissioner of his commandery, and commissioner for the Henan and Huainan mobile patrol and suppression forces.

sentences.zh: 魯炅敗於葉縣，退守南陽，乃以瑱為南陽太守、兼御史中丞，充山南東道節度防禦處置等使以代炅。

translations.literal: When Lu Jiong was defeated at Ye County and withdrew to hold Nanyang, Zhen was then made Grand Warden of Nanyang, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Shannan East circuit military commissioner for defense and disposition, among other duties, to replace Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Jiong's defeat at Ye and withdrawal to Nanyang, Zhen was made grand warden of Nanyang, concurrent vice censor-in-chief, and military commissioner of eastern Shannan with full defense powers, replacing Jiong.

sentences.zh: 尋以嗣虢王巨為御史大夫、河南節度使，因奏炅守南陽，詔各復本位。

translations.literal: Soon the Heir Apparent of the State of Guo, Prince Ju, was made Grand Censor and Henan military commissioner; [the court] thereupon memorialized that Jiong should hold Nanyang, and an edict ordered each to resume his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Prince Ju of Guo was named grand censor and Henan commissioner. The court then confirmed Jiong in the defense of Nanyang and ordered both men back to their original posts.

sentences.zh: 賊攻圍南陽累月，瑱分兵與襄陽節度使魏仲犀救之。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked and besieged Nanyang for many months; Zhen divided troops with the Xiangyang military commissioner Wei Zhongxi to rescue [Jiong].
translations.idiomatic: The rebels besieged Nanyang for months. Zhen detached troops to join the Xiangyang commissioner Wei Zhongxi in relieving the city.

sentences.zh: 犀遣弟孟馴將兵至明府橋，望風敗走，賊追蹙，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Zhongxi sent his younger brother Mengxun to command troops to Mingfu Bridge; at sight of the wind [of the enemy] they were defeated and fled; the rebels pressed in pursuit and they returned in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi sent his brother Mengxun ahead to Mingfu Bridge. At the first sight of the enemy Mengxun's force broke and fled. The rebels pressed the pursuit and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 兵素少，遇敗，人情恟懼，瑱綏撫訓練，賊不能侵。

translations.literal: Troops had always been few; encountering defeat, popular sentiment was alarmed and fearful; Zhen pacified and trained [them], and the rebels could not invade.
translations.idiomatic: His force had always been small, and the defeat spread panic. Zhen steadied and drilled his men, and the rebels could not break him.

sentences.zh: 詔為淮南西道節度使。

translations.literal: He was ordered to be Huai-Nan West circuit military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of Huai-Nan West.

sentences.zh: 收復兩京，與魯炅同制加開府儀同三司、兼御史大夫，封潁國公，食實封二百戶，余如故。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, by the same edict as Lu Jiong he was additionally made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the status of Three Excellencies, concurrent Grand Censor, enfeoffed as Duke of Ying state, with an actual fief of two hundred households; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the recovery of the two capitals he received, in the same edict as Lu Jiong, the rank of grand master of splendid happiness with the privileges of the three excellencies, concurrent grand censor, and the title duke of Ying with a fief of two hundred households; his other offices remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: ，召為殿中監。

translations.literal: [In the second year of Qianyuan,] he was summoned as Director of the Palace Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In 759 he was recalled to court as director of the palace directorate.

sentences.zh: 二年，初除涼州刺史、河南節度經略副大使。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was first appointed Grand Warden of Liangzhou and deputy grand ambassador for Henan circuit military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was first named grand warden of Liangzhou and deputy grand ambassador for Henan military strategy.

sentences.zh: 未行，屬相州官軍為史思明所敗，東京震駭。

translations.literal: Before he departed, it happened that the government forces at Xiangzhou were defeated by Shi Siming, and the Eastern Capital was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, imperial forces at Xiangzhou were routed by Shi Siming, and panic spread through the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 元帥司徒郭子儀鎮谷水，乃以瑱為陜州刺史，充陜、虢等州節度，並潼關防禦、團練、鎮守使。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal of State, Situ Guo Ziyi, held Gu River; [the court] thereupon appointed Zhen Grand Warden of Shaanzhou, made him military commissioner for Shaan, Guo, and other prefectures, and also defense, training, and garrison commissioner at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Guo Ziyi was holding Gu River, and the court then made Zhen grand warden of Shaanzhou, military commissioner over Shaan, Guo, and related prefectures, and also defense, training, and garrison commissioner at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 乾元三年四月十三日，襄州軍將張維瑾、曹玠率眾謀亂，殺刺史史翙。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the fourth month in the third year of Qianyuan, the Xiangzhou military officers Zhang Weijin and Cao Jie led their men in a plot to rebel and killed the prefect Shi Hui.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the fourth month of 760, Xiangzhou officers Zhang Weijin and Cao Jie mutinied and killed the prefect Shi Hui.

sentences.zh: 以瑱為襄州刺史、兼御史大夫，充山南東道襄、鄧、均、房、金、商、隨、郢、復十州節度觀察處置使。

translations.literal: Zhen was made Grand Warden of Xiangzhou, concurrent Grand Censor, and military observation and disposition commissioner for the ten prefectures of Xiang, Deng, Jun, Fang, Jin, Shang, Sui, Ying, and Fu in eastern Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was appointed grand warden of Xiangzhou and concurrent grand censor, with military observation and disposition authority over ten eastern Shannan prefectures from Xiang through Fu.

sentences.zh: ，肅宗召瑱入京。

translations.literal: [In the third year of Shangyuan,] Emperor Suzong summoned Zhen to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 762 Emperor Suzong summoned Zhen to the capital.

sentences.zh: 瑱樂襄州，將士亦慕瑱之政，因諷將吏、州牧、縣宰上表請留之，身赴詔命，行及鄧州，復詔歸鎮。

translations.literal: Zhen delighted in Xiangzhou, and his officers and men also admired his governance; he therefore prompted generals, officials, prefects, and magistrates to memorialize the throne asking that he remain; he himself set out to obey the summons, but when he reached Dengzhou an edict ordered him back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was happy at Xiangzhou, and his troops admired his rule. He had his officers and local officials petition the throne to keep him there, yet he himself set out to obey the summons; when he reached Dengzhou, another edict sent him back to his command.

sentences.zh: 肅宗聞其計而惡之。

translations.literal: Suzong heard of this scheme and took offense.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong learned of the maneuver, he took offense.

sentences.zh: 後呂諲、王仲昇及中官皆言瑱布恩惠，懼其得士心，以瑱為鄧州刺史，充山南東道襄、鄧、唐、復、郢、隨等六州節度，余並如故。

translations.literal: Later Lü Yin, Wang Zhongsheng, and the palace eunuchs all said that Zhen was dispensing favors and they feared he was winning the hearts of his soldiers; Zhen was made Grand Warden of Dengzhou and military commissioner of six prefectures—Xiang, Deng, Tang, Fu, Ying, and Sui—in eastern Shannan; his other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lü Yin, Wang Zhongsheng, and the palace eunuchs all warned that Zhen was buying loyalty and might win his army's hearts. He was moved to grand warden of Dengzhou with command of six eastern Shannan prefectures, while his other titles stayed unchanged.

sentences.zh: 俄而淮西節度王仲昇與賊將謝欽讓戰於申州城下，為賊所虜。

translations.literal: Soon the Huai-Xi commissioner Wang Zhongsheng fought the rebel general Xie Qinrang below Shen prefecture and was captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Huai-Xi commissioner Wang Zhongsheng fought the rebel general Xie Qinrang below Shen prefecture and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 初，仲昇被圍累月，呂諲病於江陵，瑱在襄州，又恐仲昇構己，遂顧望不救。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhongsheng had been besieged for many months, Lü Yin lay ill at Jiangling and Zhen was at Xiangzhou; fearing that Zhongsheng might frame him, he hesitated and sent no relief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhongsheng had been besieged for months while Lü Yin lay ill at Jiangling and Zhen held Xiangzhou. Fearing that Zhongsheng might frame him, Zhen held back and sent no relief.

sentences.zh: 及師出，仲昇已沒。

translations.literal: By the time his force marched out, Zhongsheng had already perished.
translations.idiomatic: By the time his troops marched out, Zhongsheng was already dead.

sentences.zh: 裴頻表陳瑱之狀，謀奪其位，稱「瑱善謀而勇，崛強難制，宜早除之，可一戰而擒也。

translations.literal: Pei Chong repeatedly memorialized the court on Zhen's conduct, plotting to seize his post, saying, "Zhen is skilled in strategy and brave, obstinate and hard to control; he should be removed early—he can be taken in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Chong repeatedly memorialized the throne about Zhen, plotting to seize his post. He said, "Zhen is clever and brave, stubborn and hard to control. Remove him early and he can be taken in one battle."

sentences.zh: 」肅宗然之，遂以瑱檢校戶部尚書、兼御史大夫、安州刺史，充淮西申、安、蘄、黃、光、沔節度觀察，兼河南陳、豫、許、鄭、汴、曹、宋、潁、泗十五州節度觀察使，外示尊崇，實奪其權也。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved; Zhen was then made acting Minister of Revenue, concurrent Grand Censor, and Prefect of Anzhou, with military observation over Shen, An, Qi, Huang, Guang, and Mian in Huai-Xi, and also military observation commissioner over fifteen Henan prefectures—Chen, Yu, Xu, Zheng, Bian, Cao, Song, Ying, and Si—outwardly an honor but in fact a stripping of his power.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed. Zhen was named acting minister of revenue, concurrent grand censor, and prefect of Anzhou, with observation over six Huai-Xi prefectures and fifteen Henan prefectures—an outward honor that in fact stripped him of power.

sentences.zh: 加裴兼御史中丞、襄鄧等七州防禦使以代之。

translations.literal: Pei Chong was additionally made Vice Censor-in-Chief and defense commissioner of seven prefectures including Xiang and Deng to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Chong was also made vice censor-in-chief and defense commissioner of seven prefectures including Xiang and Deng to replace him.

sentences.zh: 瑱懼不自安，上表稱「淮西無糧饋軍，臣去秋種得麥，請待收麥畢赴上」，復諷屬吏請留之。

translations.literal: Zhen, fearing for his safety, memorialized, "Huai-Xi has no grain to supply the army; last autumn I planted wheat; please let me wait until the harvest is complete before reporting to court," and again prompted his subordinates to ask that he remain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, uneasy and afraid, memorialized that Huai-Xi had no grain for the army, that he had planted wheat the previous autumn, and asked to wait until the harvest before reporting to court, while again prompting his subordinates to petition that he stay.

sentences.zh: 裴於商州召募，以窺去就。

translations.literal: Pei Chong recruited troops at Shangzhou to watch Zhen's movements.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Chong raised troops at Shangzhou to probe Zhen's intentions.

sentences.zh: 五月，代宗即位，因復授瑱襄州節度、奉義軍渭北兵馬等使，官如故，潛令裴圖之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, when Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Zhen was again given the Xiangzhou commission and command of the Fengyi Army's Weibei forces, with his offices as before, while the court secretly ordered Pei Chong to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, when Daizong took the throne, Zhen was restored to the Xiangzhou commission and command of the Fengyi Army's Weibei forces with his other offices unchanged, while the court secretly ordered Pei Chong to move against him.

sentences.zh: 其月十九日，裴率眾浮漢江而下。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of that month, Pei led his men downstream on the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth of that month Pei led his force down the Han River.

sentences.zh: 日暮，候者白瑱，謀於帳下，副使薛南陽曰：「尚書奉詔留鎮，裴以兵代，是無名也。

translations.literal: At dusk a lookout reported to Zhen. They deliberated in his tent; the deputy commissioner Xue Nanyang said, "You were ordered by edict to remain on post. Pei Chong is replacing you with troops—that is without just cause."
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a scout reported to Zhen. In council under his tent the deputy commissioner Xue Nanyang said, "You were ordered by edict to remain in command. Pei Chong is trying to replace you with troops—that has no proper justification."

sentences.zh: 且之智勇，非尚書敵也，眾心歸尚書，不歸於。

translations.literal: Moreover, Pei Chong's wit and courage are no match for yours, Minister; the troops' hearts are with you, not with Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Pei Chong's wit and courage are no match for yours, and the men's loyalty is with you, not with him.

sentences.zh: 彼若乘我之不虞，今夕而至，直燒城市，我眾必懼而亂，彼乘亂而擊，則可憂也。

translations.literal: If he takes advantage of our unreadiness and arrives tonight, burning the city outright, our men will surely panic and break; if he strikes amid the disorder, we will have much to fear.
translations.idiomatic: If he catches us off guard and arrives tonight, sets the city ablaze, and our men panic and scatter, then strikes in the confusion, we will be in real danger.

sentences.zh: 若及明而至，尚書破之必矣。

translations.literal: If he waits until dawn, you will surely defeat him, Minister.
translations.idiomatic: If he waits until daylight, you will surely break him.

sentences.zh: 」翌日平明，督軍士五千列於谷水北，瑱以兵逆之，登高而陣，呼將士告之曰：「爾何事來？

translations.literal: " The next day at first light Chong drilled five thousand soldiers and drew them up north of Gu River. Zhen met him with troops, formed ranks on high ground, and called to Chong's officers and men: "What business brings you here?"
translations.idiomatic: " The next day at dawn Pei Chong arrayed five thousand men north of Gu River. Zhen advanced to meet him, formed battle lines on high ground, and called to Pei's officers and men, "What brings you here?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「尚書不受命，謹奉中丞伐罪人。

translations.literal: " They answered, "The Minister refused the order; we obediently follow the vice censor-in-chief to punish a criminal."
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "The minister refused the order. We follow the vice censor-in-chief to punish a criminal."

sentences.zh: 若尚書受替，謹當釋兵。

translations.literal: If the Minister accepts replacement, we will at once lay down our arms.
translations.idiomatic: If the minister accepts replacement, we will lay down our arms at once.

sentences.zh: 」瑱曰：「恩制復除瑱此州。

translations.literal: " Zhen said, "An imperial favor has restored me to this prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen said, "An imperial favor has restored me to this prefecture."

sentences.zh: 」及取告身敕書以示，軍皆曰：「偽也。

translations.literal: " When he produced his commission and edict to show them, Chong's army all said, "It is a forgery."
translations.idiomatic: " When he produced his commission and edict, Pei's troops all cried, "It is a forgery."

sentences.zh: 承命討君，豈千里空歸，富貴在於今日。

translations.literal: We were ordered to punish you—how could we return a thousand li empty-handed? Fortune and rank lie in today's fight.
translations.idiomatic: We were ordered to punish you. How could we march a thousand li and return empty-handed? Fortune and rank are won today.

sentences.zh: 」遂爭射之。

translations.literal: " They then shot at him in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: " They then loosed a volley at him.

sentences.zh: 瑱奔歸旗下，薛南陽曰：「事急矣，請以三百騎為奇兵，尚書勿與之戰。

translations.literal: Zhen ran back to his own standards. Xue Nanyang said, "The matter is urgent. Let me take three hundred cavalry as a flanking force; Minister, do not engage them in pitched battle."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen ran back to his own lines. Xue Nanyang said, "This is urgent. Give me three hundred horsemen as a flanking force, and do not meet them in pitched battle."

sentences.zh: 」兩軍相見，遂以麾下旁萬山而出其背，表裏夾擊，軍大敗，投水而死，殺獲殆盡。

translations.literal: " When the two armies met, he led his men around by Mount Wan and struck their rear; attacked front and rear, Chong's army was smashed. Many drowned in the river; nearly all were killed or captured.
translations.idiomatic: " When the armies clashed, he took his men around Mount Wan and struck from the rear. Caught between two attacks, Pei's force was shattered. Many drowned in the river, and nearly all were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 及弟薦脫身北走，妻子並為瑱所擒，瑱甚厚撫之。

translations.literal: Pei Chong and his brother Jian escaped north on foot; their wives and children were all seized by Zhen, who treated them kindly.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Chong and his brother Jian escaped north on foot, but their wives and children were all taken by Zhen, who treated them with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 因抗表謝罪。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial pleading guilty.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial asking forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 擒於申口，送至京師，長流費州，賜死於藍田故驛。

translations.literal: Chong was taken at Shen Ford, sent to the capital, sentenced to perpetual exile in Fei prefecture, and ordered to die at the old Lantian post station.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Chong was captured at Shen Ford, sent to the capital, sentenced to perpetual exile in Fei prefecture, and ordered to die at the old Lantian post station.

sentences.zh: 八月，瑱入朝謝罪，代宗特寵異之，遷兵部尚書、同中書門下平章事，依前山南東道節度、觀察等使，代左僕射裴冕充山陵使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Zhen entered court to plead guilty. Daizong treated him with exceptional favor, promoted him to Minister of War and equitable minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery, while he continued as eastern Shannan commissioner and observer; he replaced the left vice president Pei Mian as director of the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhen came to court to plead guilty. Daizong favored him unusually, made him minister of war and equitable minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery, kept him as eastern Shannan commissioner and observer, and had him replace the left vice president Pei Mian as director of the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 時中官驃騎大將軍程元振居中用事，發瑱言涉不順，王仲昇賊平來歸，證瑱與賊合，故令仲昇陷賊三年。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuch Flying Cavalry Grand General Cheng Yuanzhen held power at court. He spread word that Zhen's remarks smacked of disloyalty; Wang Zhongsheng, after the rebels were pacified, returned and testified that Zhen had colluded with them, which was why Zhongsheng had been trapped among the rebels for three years.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eunuch Flying Cavalry Grand General Cheng Yuanzhen held power at court. He spread word that Zhen's words smacked of disloyalty, and when Wang Zhongsheng returned after the rebels were pacified he testified that Zhen had colluded with them, which was why Zhongsheng had been trapped among the rebels for three years.

sentences.zh: 代宗含怒久之，因是下詔曰：

translations.literal: Daizong nursed his anger for a long time and on that account issued an edict saying:
translations.idiomatic: Daizong nursed his anger for a long time and on that account issued an edict saying:

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，貴在於必書；

translations.literal: The principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals holds that what must be recorded must be written;
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that what must be recorded must be written;

sentences.zh: 君臣之間，法存於無赦。

translations.literal: between lord and minister the law brooks no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: between ruler and minister the law brooks no pardon.

sentences.zh: 沮勸式遵於前典，進退莫匪於至公，惡稔既彰，明罰難貸。

translations.literal: To discourage wrongdoing and encourage compliance accords with the ancient canon; advance and retreat must not stray from perfect fairness—when evil is fully manifest, clear punishment cannot be spared.
translations.idiomatic: To discourage wrongdoing and reward obedience follows the ancient canon; advance and retreat must not stray from perfect fairness—when evil is fully manifest, clear punishment cannot be spared.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司、行兵部尚書、中書門下平章事、充山南東道節度觀察處置等使、上柱國、潁國公來瑱，謬當任用，素乏器能，亟歷班榮，累經節制。

translations.literal: Lai Zhen, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the status of the Three Excellencies, acting Minister of War, equitable minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery, military observation and disposition commissioner of eastern Shannan, Pillar of State, and Duke of Ying, was rashly placed in office though he had always lacked ability; he rose swiftly through court glory and served repeatedly as a military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zhen, grand master of splendid happiness with the privileges of the three excellencies, acting minister of war, equitable minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery, eastern Shannan observation and disposition commissioner, pillar of state, and duke of Ying, was rashly entrusted with office though he had always lacked ability. He rose swiftly through court honors and served repeatedly as a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蒞職蔑聞於成績，登朝虛美於崇名。

translations.literal: In his post no achievements were heard; in court he bore only empty honor in a lofty name.
translations.idiomatic: In office he produced no achievements worth the name; in court he bore only empty honor in a lofty title.

sentences.zh: 頃者分閫頒條，久淹江、漢。

translations.literal: Recently he held a command at the frontier and long lingered on the Yangtze and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Recently he held a frontier command and long lingered on the Yangtze and Han.

sentences.zh: 或頻徵不至，或移鎮遲留，實乖堂陛之儀，爰及干戈之忿。

translations.literal: Sometimes he was summoned repeatedly and did not come; sometimes he delayed on a transfer of his post—he truly fell short of court ritual and provoked armed strife.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he was summoned repeatedly and did not come; sometimes he delayed on a transfer of post. He truly fell short of court ritual and provoked armed strife.

sentences.zh: 朕以舊臣宿將，道在含弘，會其來庭，用甄後效。

translations.literal: We regarded him as an old minister and veteran commander and meant to show forbearance; when he came to court we hoped to test his later conduct.
translations.idiomatic: We regarded him as an old minister and veteran commander and meant to show forbearance. When he came to court we hoped to test what he would do next.

sentences.zh: 超登宰輔，光拜夏卿，列在三臺，掩其一眚。

translations.literal: He was raised above measure to the chief ministry and honored as summer minister; ranked among the Three Offices, one fault was covered over.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised above measure to the chief ministry and honored as summer minister. Ranked among the Three Offices, one fault was covered over.

sentences.zh: 山陵先遠，事委近臣，謀謨素闕於大猷，卜祝頗聞於私議。

translations.literal: The imperial tombs drew near, affairs were entrusted to a close minister—yet in counsel and planning he long lacked broad strategy, and in divination and sacrifice private talk was widely heard.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tombs drew near and affairs were entrusted to a close minister, yet in counsel and planning he long lacked broad strategy, and private talk of divination and sacrifice was widely heard.

sentences.zh: 實虧周慎，且間樞言，何以輔弼鼎司，儀刑簪紱？

translations.literal: This truly fell short of thorough caution and also disturbed confidential court speech—how could he assist the tripartite stewards and be a model for the girdled ranks?
translations.idiomatic: This truly fell short of thorough caution and also disturbed confidential court speech. How could he assist the tripartite stewards and be a model for the girdled ranks?

sentences.zh: 據其所犯，合置殊科。

translations.literal: Judging by his offenses, he should receive an extraordinary sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by his offenses, he should receive an extraordinary sentence.

sentences.zh: 以嘗侍軒闥，用存寬免之辜；

translations.literal: Because he once attended the imperial audience hall, the crime of leniency is preserved;
translations.idiomatic: Because he once attended the imperial audience hall, leniency is preserved;

sentences.zh: 緬範舊章，兼膺黜削之譴。

translations.literal: invoking the old statutes, he also bears the censure of dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: invoking the old statutes, he also bears the censure of dismissal.

sentences.zh: 其身官爵，一切削除。

translations.literal: All his personal offices and titles are hereby struck away.
translations.idiomatic: All his personal offices and titles are hereby struck away.

sentences.zh: 正月，貶播州縣尉員外置。

translations.literal: In the first month he was demoted to acting assistant magistrate of Bo prefecture with supernumerary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month he was demoted to acting assistant magistrate of Bo prefecture on a supernumerary appointment.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賜死於鄠縣，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: The next day he was ordered to die at Hu County, and his household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was ordered to die at Hu County, and his household property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 瑱之被刑也，門客四散，掩於坎中。

translations.literal: When Zhen was punished his retainers scattered in all directions, and he was buried in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was executed his retainers scattered, and he was buried in a shallow pit.

sentences.zh: 校書郎殷亮後至，獨哭於屍側，貨所乘驢以備棺衾，夜詣縣令長孫演以情告之，演義而從之。

translations.literal: Later the collator Yin Liang arrived alone, wept by the corpse, sold his donkey to buy a coffin and shroud, and at night went to the magistrate Changsun Yan to explain the matter; Yan acted on principle and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the collator Yin Liang arrived alone, wept beside the corpse, sold his donkey to buy a coffin and shroud, and at night went to the magistrate Changsun Yan to explain the matter. Yan acted on principle and agreed.

sentences.zh: 亮夜葬而祭，走歸京師。

translations.literal: Liang buried him by night and offered sacrifice, then fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liang buried him by night, offered sacrifice, and fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗既悟元振之誣構，積其過而配流溱州。

translations.literal: When Daizong realized that Yuanzhen's charges were a frame-up, he tallied his offenses and banished him to Chen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong realized that Yuanzhen had framed Zhen, he tallied Yuanzhen's offenses and banished him to Chen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，瑱行軍司馬龐充統兵二千人赴河南，至汝州，聞瑱死，將士魚目等回兵襲襄州，左兵馬使李昭禦之，奔房州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhen's army marshal Sun Pangchong had led two thousand men to Henan; reaching Ru prefecture they heard of Zhen's death. Officers such as Yu Mu turned back and struck Xiangzhou; the left army commander Li Zhao repulsed them, and they fled to Fang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhen's army marshal Sun Pangchong had led two thousand men to Henan. At Ru prefecture they heard of Zhen's death. Officers such as Yu Mu turned back and attacked Xiangzhou. The left army commander Li Zhao repulsed them, and they fled to Fang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 昭及薛南陽與右兵馬使梁崇義不葉相圖，為崇義所殺。

translations.literal: Zhao, Xue Nanyang, and the right army commander Liang Chongyi could not get along and were killed by Chongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, Xue Nanyang, and the right army commander Liang Chongyi fell out with one another and were killed by Chongyi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷授崇義節度使、兼御史中丞以代瑱。

translations.literal: The court appointed Chongyi military commissioner and concurrent vice censor-in-chief to replace Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Chongyi military commissioner and concurrent vice censor-in-chief to replace Zhen.

sentences.zh: 崇義瑱立祠，四時拜饗，不居瑱廳及正堂視事，於東廂下構一小室而寢止，抗疏哀請收葬，優詔許之。

translations.literal: Chongyi built a shrine to Zhen and offered seasonal sacrifice; he did not sit in audience in Zhen's hall or main council chamber but erected a small room under the east wing to lodge in, and submitted a passionate memorial begging that Zhen be given burial—an edict graciously granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi built a shrine to Zhen and offered seasonal sacrifice. He would not conduct business in Zhen's hall or main council chamber, but built a small room under the east wing to sleep in, and submitted a passionate memorial begging that Zhen be given burial. A gracious edict granted it.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，追復官爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde his offices and titles were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 763 his offices and titles were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 周智光周智光，本以騎射從軍，常有戎捷，自行間登偏裨。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhiguang was a man who had entered the army through mounted archery, often winning on campaign, and had risen from the ranks to junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhiguang had entered the army as a mounted archer, often won on campaign, and had risen from the ranks to junior officer.

sentences.zh: 宦官魚朝恩為觀軍容使，鎮陜州，與之昵狎。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yu Chaoen was army-supervising commissioner, stationed at Shaanzhou, and was on familiar terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yu Chaoen was army-supervising commissioner, stationed at Shaanzhou, and was on intimate terms with him.

sentences.zh: 朝恩以扈從功，恩渥崇厚，奏請多允，屢於上前賞拔智光，累遷華州刺史、同華二州節度使及潼關防禦使，加檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Chaoen, for his merit in attending the emperor, received thick favor; his memorials were mostly approved, and he repeatedly praised Zhiguang before the throne until he rose through successive posts to prefect of Hua, commissioner of Tong and Hua, and Tong Pass defense commissioner, with additional acting minister of works and concurrent grand censor.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoen, for his merit in attending the emperor, received thick favor. His memorials were mostly approved, and he repeatedly praised Zhiguang before the throne until he rose through successive posts to prefect of Hua, commissioner of Tong and Hua, and Tong Pass defense commissioner, with additional acting minister of works and concurrent grand censor.

sentences.zh: ，吐蕃、回紇、党項薔、渾、奴剌十餘萬眾寇奉天、醴泉等縣，智光邀戰，破於澄城，收駝馬軍資萬計，因逐賊至鄜州。

translations.literal: [In the first year of Guangde,] more than a hundred thousand men of Tibet, the Uyghurs, the Tangut Qi, Hun, and Nulak raided Fengtian, Liquan, and other counties. Zhiguang intercepted them, defeated them at Chengcheng, took countless camels, horses, and military stores, and pursued the enemy to Bin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 763 more than a hundred thousand Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tangut Qi, Hun, and Nulak raided Fengtian, Liquan, and other counties. Zhiguang intercepted them, defeated them at Chengcheng, seized countless camels, horses, and military stores, and pursued the enemy to Bin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 智光與杜冕不協，遂殺鄜州刺史張麟，坑杜冕家屬八十一人，焚坊州廬舍三千餘家。

translations.literal: Zhiguang was at odds with Du Mian and thereupon killed the Bin prefect Zhang Lin, buried alive eighty-one members of Mian's household, and burned more than three thousand dwellings in Fang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang was at odds with Du Mian and thereupon killed the Bin prefect Zhang Lin, buried alive eighty-one members of Mian's household, and burned more than three thousand dwellings in Fang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 懼罪，召不赴命。

translations.literal: Fearing punishment, he did not answer when summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, he did not answer when summoned.

sentences.zh: 朝廷外示優容，俾杜冕使梁州，實避仇也。

translations.literal: The court outwardly showed indulgence and sent Du Mian to Liangzhou, in truth to keep him clear of his enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The court outwardly showed indulgence and sent Du Mian to Liangzhou, in truth to keep him clear of his enemy.

sentences.zh: 十二月，智光專殺前虢州刺史、兼御史中孫龐充。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Zhiguang arbitrarily killed the former Guo prefect and concurrent vice censor-in-chief Sun Pangchong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhiguang arbitrarily killed the former Guo prefect and concurrent vice censor-in-chief Sun Pangchong.

sentences.zh: 充方居缞绖，潛行，智光追而斬之。

translations.literal: Chong was still in mourning weeds and fled in secret; Zhiguang pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was still in mourning weeds and fled in secret. Zhiguang pursued and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 又劫諸節度使進奉貨物及轉運米二萬石，據州反。

translations.literal: He also seized the tribute goods that various commissioners were forwarding to the court and twenty thousand shi of transport grain, and held the prefecture in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized tribute goods that various commissioners were forwarding to the court and twenty thousand shi of transport grain, and held the prefecture in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 智光自鄜坊專殺，朝廷患之，遂聚亡命不逞之徒，眾至數萬，縱其剽掠，以結其心。

translations.literal: Since Zhiguang had been killing at will in Bin and Fang, the court was alarmed; he gathered fugitives and violent men until his following reached tens of thousands, letting them plunder freely to bind their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhiguang had been killing at will in Bin and Fang, the court was alarmed. He gathered fugitives and violent men until his following reached tens of thousands, letting them plunder freely to bind their hearts to him.

sentences.zh: 初，與陜州節度使皇甫溫不協，監軍張志斌自陜入奏，智光館給禮慢，志斌責其不肅。

translations.literal: Earlier he had been at odds with the Shaanzhou commissioner Huangfu Wen. The supervising commissioner Zhang Zhibin came from Shaan to report to court; Zhiguang lodged and entertained him with slight courtesy, and Zhibin rebuked his want of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had been at odds with the Shaanzhou commissioner Huangfu Wen. The supervising commissioner Zhang Zhibin came from Shaan to report to court. Zhiguang lodged and entertained him with slight courtesy, and Zhibin rebuked his want of respect.

sentences.zh: 智光大怒曰：「僕固懷恩豈有反狀！

translations.literal: Zhiguang flew into a rage and said, "Did Pugu Huai'en show any sign of rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang flew into a rage and said, "Did Pugu Huai'en show any sign of rebellion!

sentences.zh: 皆由爾鼠輩作福作威，懼死不敢入朝。

translations.literal: It is all because you vermin play the tyrant, fear death, and dare not enter court.
translations.idiomatic: It is all because you vermin play the tyrant, fear death, and dare not enter court.

sentences.zh: 我本不反，今為爾作之。

translations.literal: I never meant to rebel, but now I rebel because of you.
translations.idiomatic: I never meant to rebel, but now I rebel because of you.

sentences.zh: 」因叱下斬之，臠其肉以飼從者。

translations.literal: " He then shouted to bring Zhibin down and behead him, carved his flesh, and fed it to his followers.
translations.idiomatic: " He then shouted to bring Zhibin down and behead him, carved his flesh, and fed it to his followers.

sentences.zh: 時淮南節度使、檢校右僕射崔圓入覲，方物百萬，智光強留其半。

translations.literal: At that time the Huainan commissioner and acting right vice president Cui Yuan was entering court with local products worth a million; Zhiguang forcibly kept half.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Huainan commissioner and acting right vice president Cui Yuan was entering court with local products worth a million. Zhiguang forcibly kept half.

sentences.zh: 舉選之士竦駭，或竊同州路以過，智光使部將邀斬於乾坑店，橫死者眾。

translations.literal: Candidates for office were terrified; some stole along the Tongzhou road to pass through. Zhiguang sent his officers to waylay and kill them at Qian'eng Station, and many died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates for office were terrified. Some stole along the Tongzhou road to pass through. Zhiguang sent his officers to waylay and kill them at Qian'eng Station, and many died on the road.

sentences.zh: 優詔以智光為尚書左僕射，遣中使余元仙持告身以授之。

translations.literal: A gracious edict made Zhiguang left vice president of the secretariat; the court sent the envoy Yu Yuanxian to present his commission in person.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict made Zhiguang left vice president of the secretariat. The court sent the envoy Yu Yuanxian to present his commission in person.

sentences.zh: 智光受詔慢罵曰：「智光有數子，皆彎弓二百斤，有萬人敵，堪出將入相。

translations.literal: Zhiguang accepted the edict with insults and curses: "Zhiguang has several sons who can each draw a two-hundred-jin bow and are a match for ten thousand men—they can serve as generals abroad and ministers at home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang accepted the edict with insults and curses: "Zhiguang has several sons who can each draw a two-hundred-jin bow and are a match for ten thousand men. They can serve as generals abroad and ministers at home.

sentences.zh: 只如挾天子令諸侯。

translations.literal: It is just like holding the Son of Heaven hostage to command the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: It is just like holding the Son of Heaven hostage to command the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 天下只有周智光合作。

translations.literal: In all the realm only Zhou Zhiguang is fit for that role.
translations.idiomatic: In all the realm only Zhou Zhiguang is fit for that role.

sentences.zh: 」因歷數大臣之過。

translations.literal: " He then went through the faults of the chief ministers one by one.
translations.idiomatic: " He then went through the faults of the chief ministers one by one.

sentences.zh: 元仙股怵，智光增絹百匹遣之。

translations.literal: Yuanxian was terrified; Zhiguang added a hundred bolts of silk and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian was terrified. Zhiguang added a hundred bolts of silk and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 於州郭置生祠，俾將吏百姓祈禱。

translations.literal: He set up a living shrine in the prefectural city and ordered officers, clerks, and common people to pray there.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a living shrine in the prefectural city and ordered officers, clerks, and common people to pray there.

sentences.zh: 正月，密詔關內河東副元帥、中書令郭子儀率兵討智光，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the first month a secret edict ordered Guo Ziyi, deputy commander of Guannei and Hedong and chief minister of the Secretariat, to lead troops against Zhiguang with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month a secret edict ordered Guo Ziyi, deputy commander of Guannei and Hedong and chief minister of the Secretariat, to lead troops against Zhiguang with authority to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 時同、華路絕，上召子儀女婿工部侍郎趙縱受口詔付子儀，縱裂帛寫詔置蠟丸中，遣家童間道達焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Tong-Hua road was cut; the emperor summoned Guo Ziyi's son-in-law Zhao Zong, vice minister of works, to receive an oral edict to deliver to Ziyi. Zong wrote the edict on cloth, sealed it in a wax pellet, and sent a household servant by a bypath to reach him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tong-Hua road was cut. The emperor summoned Guo Ziyi's son-in-law Zhao Zong, vice minister of works, to receive an oral edict for Ziyi. Zong wrote the edict on cloth, sealed it in a wax pellet, and sent a household servant by a bypath to reach him.

sentences.zh: 子儀奉詔將出師，華州將士相顧攜貳。

translations.literal: Ziyi received the order and was about to march; the Hua prefecture troops looked at one another with divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi received the order and was about to march. The Hua prefecture troops looked at one another with divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 智光大將李漢惠自同州以其所管降子儀。

translations.literal: Zhiguang's great general Li Huihui came from Tong prefecture with his command and surrendered to Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang's great general Li Huihui came from Tong prefecture with his command and surrendered to Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 貶智光為澧州刺史，散官勛封如故。

translations.literal: Zhiguang was demoted to prefect of Li; his honorary rank, fief, and seal remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang was demoted to prefect of Li. His honorary rank, fief, and seal remained as before.

sentences.zh: 乃聽將一百人隨身，便路赴任，其所部將士官吏，一無所問。

translations.literal: He was allowed to take only a hundred men with him and proceed by the nearest route to his post; his subordinate officers, soldiers, and clerks were none of them questioned.
translations.idiomatic: He was allowed to take only a hundred men with him and proceed by the nearest route to his post. His subordinate officers, soldiers, and clerks were none of them questioned.

sentences.zh: 乃以兵部侍郎張仲光為華州刺史、兼御史大夫、潼關防禦使；

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongguang, vice minister of war, was made prefect of Hua, concurrent grand censor, and Tong Pass defense commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongguang, vice minister of war, was made prefect of Hua, concurrent grand censor, and Tong Pass defense commissioner;

sentences.zh: 又以大理卿敬括為同州刺史、兼御史大夫、長春宮等使。

translations.literal: Jing Kuo, grand judge of the Court of Judicial Review, was made prefect of Tong, concurrent grand censor, and commissioner of Changchun Palace and other duties.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Kuo, grand judge of the Court of Judicial Review, was made prefect of Tong, concurrent grand censor, and commissioner of Changchun Palace and other duties.

sentences.zh: 是日，智光為帳下將斬首，並子元耀、元幹等二人來獻。

translations.literal: That same day Zhiguang was beheaded by an officer of his own tent, and his sons Yuanyao and Yuangan were also brought forward as trophies.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Zhiguang was beheaded by an officer of his own tent, and his sons Yuanyao and Yuangan were also brought forward as trophies.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，梟智光首於皇城之南街，二子腰斬以示眾。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao his head was displayed on the south street of the Imperial City; his two sons were cut in two at the waist to warn the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingmao his head was displayed on the south street of the Imperial City. His two sons were cut in two at the waist to warn the crowd.

sentences.zh: 判官監察御史邵賁、都虞候蔣羅漢並伏誅，餘黨各以親疏準法定罪。

translations.literal: The administrative aide, investigating censor Shao Fen, and the commandant of justice Jiang Luohan were both executed by law; the remaining partisans were each sentenced according to the statutes, in proportion to their closeness or distance [from the crime].
translations.idiomatic: The investigating censor and aide Shao Fen and the commandant of justice Jiang Luohan were both executed, and the remaining conspirators were sentenced according to law by degree of complicity.

sentences.zh: 命有司具儀奏告太清宮、太廟、七陵。

translations.literal: The responsible offices were ordered to prepare the rites and memorialize the report to the Supreme Pure Palace, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the seven imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the proper rites performed and the victory reported to the Supreme Pure Palace, the ancestral temple, and the seven imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 時淮西節度使李忠臣入觀，次潼關，聞智光阻兵，駐所部將往禦之。

translations.literal: At that time the Huai-Nan West military commissioner Li Zhongchen was entering court for audience and halted at Tong Pass; hearing that Zhiguang was blocking the army with arms, he halted his command and was about to go to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen, military commissioner of Huai-Nan West, was then on his way to court and paused at Tong Pass. Learning that Zhiguang had taken up arms, he halted his troops to march against him.

sentences.zh: 及智光死，忠臣進兵入華州大掠，自赤水至潼關二百里間，畜產財物殆盡，官吏至有著紙衣或數日不食者。

translations.literal: When Zhiguang died, Zhongchen advanced his army into Hua prefecture and plundered on a great scale; from Chishui to Tong Pass, within two hundred li, livestock and goods were nearly exhausted; officials even came to wear paper clothing or go several days without eating.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhiguang's death Zhongchen marched into Hua and looted the region from Chishui to Tong Pass for two hundred li, stripping it nearly bare. Some officials were reduced to wearing paper clothes or going days without food.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：嘗讀《李陵傳》，戰敗不能死，屈節降虜庭，君不得為忠臣，母不得為孝子，每長嘆久之。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The historiographer says: I once read the biography of Li Ling—defeated in battle yet unable to die, bending his integrity to submit in the barbarian court, so that as a subject he could not be a loyal minister and as a son he could not be a filial son; each time I have sighed long over this.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: I once read the biography of Li Ling. Defeated yet unwilling to die, he bowed to the enemy and so failed both his sovereign as a loyal minister and his mother as a filial son. I have sighed over that story many times.

sentences.zh: 炅收滍水敗眾，守南陽孤城，每蹈危機，竟效死節，料敵雖非其良將，事君不失為忠臣。

translations.literal: Jiong gathered the defeated masses at the Zhi River, held the lone city of Nanyang, repeatedly trod on critical peril, and in the end displayed the integrity of death; though in estimating the enemy he was not an excellent general, in serving his lord he did not fail to be a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong rallied the shattered army from the Zhi River disaster and held lonely Nanyang through repeated crises until he gave his life. He was no master of strategy, but in loyalty to his sovereign he did not fail.

sentences.zh: 浮躁無行，狂悖用兵，宜其死矣。

translations.literal: [Pei Chong was] flighty and shallow in conduct, reckless and perverse in wielding arms—his death was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Chong was frivolous and unprincipled and waged war with mad violence. He deserved his end.

sentences.zh: 瑱善軍政，得士心，庶幾幹城禦侮者哉！

translations.literal: Zhen was skilled in military government and won the hearts of the troops—he might almost have been one who shields the state and repels insult!
translations.idiomatic: Zhen excelled in military administration and won the loyalty of his men. He might have been a true bulwark of the realm.

sentences.zh: 始固名位，為裴巧言；

translations.literal: At first he secured name and position through Pei [Chong]'s clever words;
translations.idiomatic: At first he secured his position through Pei Chong's clever intrigues;

sentences.zh: 終歸朝廷，遭元振誣構。

translations.literal: in the end he returned to the court and was framed by Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: yet when he returned to court he was destroyed by Cheng Yuanzhen's false accusations.

sentences.zh: 賜死之辜匪辨，用刑之道不明。

translations.literal: The guilt for which he was granted death was not distinguished, and the way of applying punishment was not clear.
translations.idiomatic: His guilt was never properly examined, and the principles of justice were obscured.

sentences.zh: 致舊將立祠，門吏偷葬，出將入相，一至於斯，惜哉！

translations.literal: The result was that old officers raised a shrine, gate clerks secretly buried him—a man who went out as general and entered as chancellor reduced to this: alas!
translations.idiomatic: Old officers built him a shrine; a gate clerk gave him a secret burial. A man who had risen from general to chief minister came to this—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 智光狂悖，不足與論。

translations.literal: Zhiguang was mad and perverse—not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguang was a mad rebel, scarcely worth mention.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：魯炅竭節，來瑱枉死。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Lu Jiong exhausted his integrity; Lai Zhen died wrongfully.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Lu Jiong gave his life in loyal service; Lai Zhen was put to death unjustly.

sentences.zh: 裴兇人，智光逆子。

translations.literal: Pei [Chong was] a violent man; Zhiguang [was] a rebellious son.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Chong was a villain; Zhou Zhiguang was a traitor.
